messages.author: 603a4ed77d3ef581
messages.subject: Specifying joint mixture models
parts:
Hi,

I would like to fit joint growth mixture models to determine life-history trajectories in mammal populations. I am interested in knowing if the probability that individuals belong to a cluster depends on three different responses (i.e. mass gain, reproduction probability and survival probability). A joint mixture model would thus separate individuals into k-clusters based on similarities in the three responses (similar to the figure below created from a model specified with the FlexMix R package in Hamel et al. 2016) .



Can a joint clustering probability be estimated for multiple responses of different families (e.g. gaussian and binomial) in R-inla?  

Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specifying joint mixture models
parts:
I'm not completely sure what you ask for, but mixture models for the
likelihood is not yet implemented, although it could be if there is a
spesific well defined case. [ie, its hard to write something 'stable'
for the general case]

H
